note: The Pattern Decoder's own data, copied verbatim out of content/prose/_raw/playbook.html. Regenerate with design/extract-playbook-data.py --apply. Nothing here is summarised or reworded.

compendium.name: Gaslighting
compendium.what: Denying someone's perception or memory to make them doubt their own mind.
compendium.why: Repeated reality-denial erodes a person's trust in their own judgment.
compendium.healthy: "I remember it differently — can we compare notes on what happened?"
sounds: That never happened.
You're imagining things again.
nots: One-off disagreement about facts is normal; people genuinely misremember. It's the *pattern* of attacking your sanity that matters.

compendium.name: Countering
compendium.what: Flatly contradicting the other person's account of events.
compendium.why: Constant contradiction makes shared reality impossible to establish.
compendium.healthy: "My memory of that is different. Let's check the messages."
sounds: You're remembering it wrong.
That's not what happened and you know it.
nots: Sometimes people truly didn't say the thing — a factual dispute is not manipulation by itself.

compendium.name: Trivializing
compendium.what: Framing the other person's reaction as excessive or silly.
compendium.why: Teaches the target their feelings are defective and not worth raising.
compendium.healthy: "I didn't realize this hit you that hard — tell me more."
sounds: You're way too sensitive.
You can't take a joke.
nots: Occasionally people do overreact, and saying so once, gently, can be honest feedback.

compendium.name: Diverting
compendium.what: Derailing the topic to avoid engaging with the actual complaint.
compendium.why: The issue never gets addressed, so it can never be repaired.
compendium.healthy: "This is hard to hear, but go ahead — I'm listening."
sounds: Why are you bringing this up now?
There you go, changing the subject to your feelings.
nots: Fatigue with a recurring argument is human; "here we go again" can be exhaustion, not strategy.

compendium.name: Selective Memory
compendium.what: Conveniently not remembering things that were said or agreed.
compendium.why: Erases commitments and past harm from the shared record.
compendium.healthy: "I honestly don't remember — can you remind me what I said?"
sounds: I never said that.
You must be confusing me with someone else.
nots: People genuinely forget things constantly. Only a *convenient* pattern of forgetting is a flag.

compendium.name: Moving Goalposts
compendium.what: Changing the success criteria after they've been met.
compendium.why: Makes approval permanently unreachable, keeping the target striving.
compendium.healthy: "You did what I asked. I realize I now also need X — that's new, and I own that."
sounds: That's still not good enough.
Now do it properly this time.
nots: Requirements legitimately change sometimes; one revision is not a trap.

compendium.name: Thought-Stopping Clichés
compendium.what: Stock phrases that shut down examination of a problem.
compendium.why: Blocks legitimate questions before they can be thought through.
compendium.healthy: "I don't have an answer, but your question is fair."
sounds: It is what it is, drop it.
Everything happens for a reason, stop dwelling.
nots: These are everyday idioms most people use with zero intent to control anything.

compendium.name: Normalization
compendium.what: Framing harmful treatment as ordinary and unquestionable.
compendium.why: Recalibrates the target's sense of what treatment is acceptable.
compendium.healthy: "This is how I've always done it, but that doesn't make it right — let's look at it."
sounds: Every couple fights like this.
This is just how families are.
nots: Sometimes the thing really is normal, and the speaker is offering perspective, not cover.

compendium.name: Guilt-Tripping
compendium.what: Inducing guilt to make refusal feel morally wrong.
compendium.why: Converts the target's conscience into a lever against them.
compendium.healthy: "I'm disappointed, and I also know it's your decision to make."
sounds: After everything I've done for you.
I never ask you for anything.
nots: Expressing genuine hurt or disappointment is healthy — the flag is guilt used to override a stated 'no'.

compendium.name: Emotional Blackmail
compendium.what: Making love or the relationship conditional on compliance.
compendium.why: Turns affection into a hostage; choice under threat isn't choice.
compendium.healthy: "This matters a lot to me. Can we find something that works for both of us?"
sounds: If you really loved me, you'd stay.
Leave, and everyone will know what you did.
nots: Stating that a behavior is a dealbreaker for you can be a legitimate boundary — context decides.

compendium.name: Self-Harm Threats as Leverage
compendium.what: Threatening self-harm to prevent the other person's exit or refusal.
compendium.why: Maximum-pressure coercion; also, any self-harm mention deserves real-world support regardless of intent — encourage involving a professional or crisis service.
compendium.healthy: "I'm in a bad place and I need support — I'll reach out to someone who can help."
sounds: If you leave, I'll hurt myself.
I'll kill myself if you go — it'll be on you.
nots: The person may genuinely be in crisis rather than strategizing — which is exactly why outside professional support, not solo management, is the right response either way.

compendium.name: Pity Plays
compendium.what: Performing helplessness or victimhood to redirect sympathy.
compendium.why: Ends accountability conversations by making the target the comforter.
compendium.healthy: "I feel awful about this, and that's mine to sit with. You were right to raise it."
sounds: Nobody has ever suffered like I have.
You'd abandon me too, like everyone else.
nots: This can be genuine low self-worth or depression speaking, not a tactic — especially outside conflict.

compendium.name: Martyrdom Display
compendium.what: Advertising one's sacrifices to generate obligation.
compendium.why: Creates a debt the target never agreed to and can never repay.
compendium.healthy: "I'm overloaded and I need help — can you take X?"
sounds: I guess I'll just do everything myself, as usual.
Don't mind me, I'll sit here alone.
nots: Sometimes people really are unappreciated and are clumsily saying so.

compendium.name: Duty Scripts
compendium.what: Invoking role obligations ('a good son would…') to compel behavior.
compendium.why: Replaces the target's judgment with an unappealable rulebook.
compendium.healthy: "I'd love your help with this — no pressure if you can't."
sounds: A good daughter would never say that.
Family comes first — you owe us this.
nots: Cultural and family norms are real values for many people; invoking one isn't automatically coercive.

compendium.name: Demand for Gratitude
compendium.what: Requiring displays of thanks as payment for help given.
compendium.why: Turns generosity into a transaction with interest.
compendium.healthy: "It stung a little that the effort went unmentioned — a thank-you means a lot to me."
sounds: A thank-you would be nice for once.
You should be grateful I put up with you.
nots: Wishing to feel appreciated is universal; a single mention is a feeling, not a lever.

compendium.name: Favor Debt
compendium.what: Citing past gifts or support as grounds for present compliance.
compendium.why: Reframes past kindness as a contract the target unknowingly signed.
compendium.healthy: "I've supported you a lot and I'm asking for support back — as a request, not a bill."
sounds: Remember who paid for your school.
You owe me after everything.
nots: Reminding someone of real support during a fairness dispute can be legitimate context.

compendium.name: Catastrophizing as Control
compendium.what: Predicting the target's ruin without the speaker.
compendium.why: Installs fear of independence, making leaving feel impossible.
compendium.healthy: "I worry about how you'd manage — but that's my anxiety, and it's your life."
sounds: If you take that job, this family falls apart.
You'll end up alone and broke without me.
nots: Genuine worry about a loved one's readiness can sound similar; frequency and function distinguish them.

compendium.name: Love Bombing
compendium.what: Overwhelming early affection and idealization.
compendium.why: Builds fast dependency and sets up devaluation later.
compendium.healthy: Affection that grows at the pace of actual knowledge of the person.
sounds: You're my soulmate — I knew it the moment we met.
I've never loved anyone the way I love you.
nots: People in love genuinely talk like this. It's only a flag when intensity is disproportionate to how long or well they know you — this tool can't see that.

compendium.name: Exclusive Meaning
compendium.what: Claiming to be the only one who truly understands the target.
compendium.why: Quietly devalues every other relationship the target has.
compendium.healthy: "I feel really close to you" — without demoting everyone else.
sounds: No one will ever understand you like I do.
What we have is beyond other people.
nots: Deep intimacy sometimes honestly feels this way; said once, it's romance, not strategy.

compendium.name: Conditional Love
compendium.what: Making affection explicitly contingent on obedience.
compendium.why: Teaches the target that love must be earned by compliance.
compendium.healthy: "I'm upset with you right now, and I still love you."
sounds: I could really love you if you just lost the attitude.
Be sweet like before and we'll be fine.
nots: Hard to say innocently in this direct form — but it may be a heated exaggeration the speaker regrets.

compendium.name: Hoovering
compendium.what: Pulling the target back after distance or a breakup with promises of change.
compendium.why: Resets the cycle without any of the change actually happening.
compendium.healthy: Demonstrated change over time, before asking for another chance.
sounds: I've changed, give me one more chance.
I can't stop thinking about what we had.
nots: People do sometimes genuinely change and sincerely ask for another chance — the evidence is behavior over time, not the words.

compendium.name: Future Faking
compendium.what: Promising a future that keeps the target invested now.
compendium.why: The promised future perpetually recedes while the present costs accumulate.
compendium.healthy: Small kept promises now, instead of large deferred ones.
sounds: Next year will be different, I swear.
Once I get the promotion, then we'll travel like you want.
nots: Most future promises are sincere. This only matters as a *pattern* of promises consistently replacing action.

compendium.name: Negging
compendium.what: Backhanded compliments that lower the target's confidence.
compendium.why: Installs insecurity that makes the speaker's approval feel necessary.
compendium.healthy: A compliment with no asterisk.
sounds: You're pretty smart for someone like you.
I love that you don't care how you look.
nots: Clumsy compliments and awkward teasing exist; a single instance may be social ineptness.

compendium.name: Silent Treatment
compendium.what: Withdrawing contact as punishment until the target complies.
compendium.why: Weaponizes connection itself; the target is starved into apology.
compendium.healthy: "I'm too angry to talk right now. I need until tomorrow, then let's resolve this."
sounds: I'm not speaking to you until you apologize.
Don't talk to me. Figure out what you did.
nots: Needing space after a fight is healthy. The flag is silence with *conditions attached* — comply and I'll return.
Taking agreed time to cool off before continuing is regulation, not punishment — the difference is whether return is promised.

compendium.name: Isolation
compendium.what: Undermining the target's other relationships to increase dependence.
compendium.why: Removes the outside perspectives and support needed to see the situation clearly.
compendium.healthy: "I feel tense around your friend — but your friendships are yours."
sounds: Your friends are toxic — they're against us.
You don't need your family, you have me.
nots: Occasionally a friend really is harmful, and the concern is accurate. Ask: does this person object to *specific behavior*, or to you having other bonds at all?

compendium.name: Monitoring & Surveillance
compendium.what: Demanding access, proof, and constant accounting of the target's activity.
compendium.why: Replaces trust with inspection; the target lives under audit.
compendium.healthy: "I've been feeling insecure — can we talk about it?" (a feeling, not a search warrant).
sounds: Send me a picture right now so I know where you are.
Who were you texting? Show me your phone.
nots: A single anxious check-in during a scary moment isn't surveillance; routine demanded proof is.
Coordinating logistics ('where are you? the movie starts') is normal; the flag is demand, proof, and suspicion.

compendium.name: Location Tracking
compendium.what: Requiring live location as a condition of peace.
compendium.why: Normalizes total observability and punishes autonomy.
compendium.healthy: Optional location-sharing both people genuinely want, revocable without a fight.
sounds: Why is your location off?
Keep your location on or we have a problem.
nots: Many couples and families share location by mutual, revocable consent — the flag is *demand plus penalty*.

compendium.name: Behavior Control
compendium.what: Issuing rules about clothing, movement, or association.
compendium.why: Converts a partner or relative into a subject with a rulebook.
compendium.healthy: "That outfit makes me feel insecure — that's my thing to work on."
sounds: You're not wearing that.
You're not going unless I say so.
nots: Parents of minors legitimately set some rules; between adults this phrasing rarely has an innocent read, but heated exaggeration exists.

compendium.name: Infantilization
compendium.what: Treating a capable adult as unable to manage their own affairs.
compendium.why: Erodes self-trust until the target believes they truly can't cope.
compendium.healthy: "Want help with this, or do you have it?"
sounds: You can't handle money, sweetie, let me.
You'd be lost without me organizing your life.
nots: Can be misdirected protectiveness, especially from parents who haven't updated their picture of you.

compendium.name: "I Know Best" Paternalism
compendium.what: Overriding the target's choices 'for their own good'.
compendium.why: Dressing control as care makes it harder to refuse.
compendium.healthy: "Here's my concern. You decide — I'll back you either way."
nots: Sometimes elders genuinely do know better on a specific matter; advice becomes control only when refusal is punished.

compendium.name: Punishment of Boundaries
compendium.what: Retaliating when the target sets a limit.
compendium.why: Teaches that boundaries cost more than compliance, so they stop being set.
compendium.healthy: "Your limit stings, and I'll respect it."
sounds: Fine. Have your 'boundary.' See how the weekend goes.
Oh, you need space? Enjoy silence then.
nots: An initial hurt reaction to a new boundary is human; it's the sustained retaliation that's the flag.

compendium.name: DARVO
compendium.what: Deny, Attack, Reverse Victim and Offender — flipping the accusation.
compendium.why: The person raising harm ends up defending themselves instead.
compendium.healthy: "Let me hear the whole complaint before I respond."
sounds: Oh, so now I'm the villain?
I can't believe you're attacking me after what YOU did.
nots: Sometimes the counter-accusation is actually true — both people can have valid grievances. Check whether the original complaint ever gets addressed.

compendium.name: Blame-Shifting
compendium.what: Relocating responsibility for one's actions onto the target.
compendium.why: The person harmed carries both the injury and the fault for it.
compendium.healthy: "I did that, and it was wrong — regardless of what led up to it."
sounds: Look what you made me do.
This is all your fault.
nots: Context genuinely matters in conflicts; naming a real contributing factor once isn't the same as refusing all ownership.

compendium.name: Whataboutism
compendium.what: Answering an accusation with a counter-accusation.
compendium.why: Ensures no complaint is ever processed — every thread ends in a draw.
compendium.healthy: "I'll answer for mine, and then I'd like to talk about yours separately."
sounds: What about that time YOU forgot?
And you're perfect, I suppose?
nots: Pointing out a genuine double standard can be fair — if the original issue still gets addressed afterward.

compendium.name: Non-Apology Apology
compendium.what: An apology for your reaction instead of their action.
compendium.why: Simulates repair while conceding nothing, closing the issue unresolved.
compendium.healthy: "I'm sorry I did X. It was wrong and I'll do Y differently."
sounds: I'm sorry you feel that way.
I'm sorry, but you started it.
nots: Some people were never taught how to apologize and sincerely believe this is one.

compendium.name: Denial
compendium.what: Blanket refusal of any wrongdoing.
compendium.why: Repair is impossible when nothing is ever admitted.
compendium.healthy: "Parts of that are fair, parts I see differently — let's go through it."
sounds: I did absolutely nothing wrong.
I have nothing to apologize for.
nots: Occasionally people are, in fact, being wrongly accused.

compendium.name: Minimization
compendium.what: Shrinking the harm so the reaction looks disproportionate.
compendium.why: If nothing is ever a big deal, nothing ever has to change.
compendium.healthy: "I hear that this landed harder than I intended — walk me through it."
sounds: You're overreacting.
It's really not that big a deal.
nots: Sometimes things genuinely aren't a big deal, and the speaker is offering (unwanted) perspective, not erasing harm.

compendium.name: Tone Policing
compendium.what: Making the delivery the issue so the content never gets heard.
compendium.why: The complaint dies in a debate about volume.
compendium.healthy: "I want to hear this — can we take ten minutes and restart calmer?" (and then actually restart).
sounds: Watch your tone.
I'm not discussing anything while you're like this.
nots: Asking to pause a genuinely heated conversation is healthy — it becomes tone policing when the content is never returned to.
Pausing a genuinely abusive shouting match is self-protection; the flag is using tone to permanently dodge the topic.

compendium.name: Kafka Trapping
compendium.what: Treating denial itself as proof of guilt.
compendium.why: Constructs an accusation that cannot be answered — every response convicts.
compendium.healthy: "Your denial doesn't prove anything either way — let's look at what actually happened."
sounds: Denying it just proves you did it.
Only a guilty person would get this defensive.
nots: Rarely innocent as phrased, but people repeat this fallacy without noticing the trap it builds.

compendium.name: Contempt
compendium.what: Expressing disgust at the person, not the behavior.
compendium.why: The single strongest predictor of relationship destruction; attacks worth, not conduct.
compendium.healthy: "What you did made me furious" — the act, not the human.
sounds: You're pathetic.
You disgust me.
nots: Words said in white-hot anger sometimes exceed what the speaker believes; a pattern is the signal.

compendium.name: Name-Calling Disguised as Humor
compendium.what: Insults delivered with a 'just joking' escape hatch.
compendium.why: Hurts on impact while making objection look humorless.
compendium.healthy: Teasing that the *target* also finds funny — and stops instantly on request.
sounds: Relax, 'idiot' is a pet name.
Can't you take a joke, drama queen?
nots: Humor styles genuinely differ; one mismatched joke plus a real apology is just friction.

compendium.name: Comparative Devaluation
compendium.what: Unfavorably measuring the target against others.
compendium.why: Installs a permanent sense of insufficiency.
compendium.healthy: "Here's what I need more of" — stated directly, no third party required.
sounds: Why can't you be more like your sister?
My ex never made this kind of scene.
nots: Sometimes a comparison is a clumsy attempt to point at a concrete example of what they're asking for.

compendium.name: Emotional Invalidation
compendium.what: Ruling the target's feelings inadmissible.
compendium.why: People who can't get feelings acknowledged stop reporting them — and stop trusting them.
compendium.healthy: "I don't fully get it, but I believe you that it hurts."
sounds: You have no reason to be upset.
Stop being so dramatic — nothing happened.
nots: A speaker may be disputing the *interpretation* of events, and phrasing it badly as a verdict on the feeling.

compendium.name: Shame Installation
compendium.what: Attacking the target's fundamental adequacy as a person.
compendium.why: Shame generalizes — it stops being about the act and becomes about the self.
compendium.healthy: "That behavior was not okay" — specific, bounded, repairable.
sounds: You should be ashamed of yourself.
What is wrong with you?
nots: 'What's wrong with you' is also a common exasperated idiom with no deeper campaign behind it.

compendium.name: Intimidation
compendium.what: Implied or explicit threat of consequences for non-compliance.
compendium.why: Compliance under threat is fear, not agreement — and it escalates.
compendium.healthy: There is no healthy version of a threat; the alternative is a request.
sounds: You don't want to see me angry.
Keep pushing and find out what happens.
nots: Very hard to read innocently — though 'you'll regret this' occasionally means 'I predict you'll wish otherwise', not a threat.

compendium.name: Triangulation
compendium.what: Recruiting real or invented third parties as ammunition.
compendium.why: Turns a two-person disagreement into an ambush by a crowd.
compendium.healthy: "Here's *my* problem with it" — owned, first-person, no chorus.
sounds: Even your mother thinks you're out of line.
Dana told me what you said about me.
nots: Citing that others share a concern can be legitimate (an intervention is triangulation-shaped but caring). Verify the chorus exists.

compendium.name: Forced Teaming
compendium.what: Manufacturing a 'we' to erase the target's separate choice.
compendium.why: Obligations get created that the target never actually agreed to.
compendium.healthy: "I'd like us to approach this together — are you in?"
sounds: We're in this together whether you like it or not.
People like us have to stick together.
nots: Team language is everywhere and almost always benign; the flag is 'we' immediately followed by *your* obligation.

compendium.name: "We're Family" Erasure
compendium.what: Using the family bond to nullify boundaries or fairness.
compendium.why: 'Family' becomes a word that means the target can't say no.
compendium.healthy: "We're family, so let's find something that's fair to both of us."
nots: Appeals to family closeness are usually sincere expressions of value, not levers.

compendium.name: Concern Trolling
compendium.what: Packaging control directives as worry.
compendium.why: Refusing 'help' gets reframed as self-destructiveness, trapping the target.
compendium.healthy: "I'm worried. Do you want my input, or just support?"
sounds: I'm only saying this because I worry about you.
As your friend, I have to say everyone's noticed.
nots: Most concern is real concern. The test: does the 'worry' only ever point toward what the speaker wants?

compendium.name: Ultimatums
compendium.what: Forcing a binary choice under threat of loss.
compendium.why: Manufactures crisis to bypass negotiation.
compendium.healthy: "This is really important to me — can we find a way through it together?"
sounds: It's me or them. Choose.
Do this or we're done.
nots: 'If you keep hurting me, I will leave' is a boundary, not an ultimatum — conditions about one's own safety or respect are legitimate.
'If you keep yelling at me, I'm leaving' is a boundary about one's own safety, not an ultimatum — this tool treats it as such.

compendium.name: Urgency Manufacturing
compendium.what: Compressing time so the target can't think or consult.
compendium.why: Deliberation is the enemy of coercion; urgency removes it.
compendium.healthy: "No rush — take the time you need and tell me tomorrow."
sounds: Decide right now or forget it.
This offer is gone by tonight.
nots: Some deadlines are real. Ask what actually happens if you take one more day.

compendium.name: False Dilemma
compendium.what: Presenting two options when more exist.
compendium.why: Hides the exits; the target chooses between traps.
compendium.healthy: "Here are the options I see — what am I missing?"
sounds: Either you trust me completely or this means nothing.
You're with me or against me.
nots: Sometimes the speaker genuinely can't see other options either.

compendium.name: Sunk Cost Exploitation
compendium.what: Using past investment to block present exit.
compendium.why: Years already spent become the reason to spend more.
compendium.healthy: "We've built a lot — I want to fight for it. Do you?" (an invitation, not a debt).
sounds: You'd throw away five years over this?
After everything we've built, you'd just walk?
nots: Grief about potentially losing shared history is genuine and human; it's exploitation only when deployed to trap.

compendium.name: Response-Time Policing
compendium.what: Treating reply latency as an offense requiring explanation.
compendium.why: Puts the target permanently on-call; delay becomes guilt.
compendium.healthy: "I get anxious when I don't hear back — a quick 'busy, later' helps me a lot."
sounds: Why did it take you two hours to reply?
Seen at 3:41. It's now 4. Explain.
nots: Feeling neglected is a real feeling; asking about it once is communication, not policing.

compendium.name: Exaggeration
compendium.what: Absolutes — 'you always', 'you never' — that inflate the claim.
compendium.why: Makes the accusation unanswerable and the fight about the word, not the issue.
compendium.healthy: "The last three times, X happened" — specific and checkable.
sounds: You ALWAYS do this.
You NEVER listen to me.
nots: Always/never is ordinary frustration language that nearly everyone uses. Alone, it means very little.
'Always/never' in venting or banter is human hyperbole; alone it means very little — this tool caps how much it can count.

compendium.name: Vague Allegations
compendium.what: Referencing unnamed critics or unspecified accusations.
compendium.why: Can't be answered or verified — an unfalsifiable smear.
compendium.healthy: "Here is who said what, specifically."
sounds: People are talking about you.
Everyone knows what you're really like.
nots: Sometimes people are awkwardly protecting a source while relaying a real concern.

compendium.name: Identity Hooking
compendium.what: Claiming ownership of the target's identity or achievements.
compendium.why: If they made you, leaving means unmaking yourself.
compendium.healthy: "I'm proud of what I contributed to your growth" — contribution, not ownership.
sounds: You'd be nothing without me.
No one else would ever put up with you.
nots: Almost never innocent as phrased; at best a grandiose overstatement of real support given.

compendium.name: Conditional Worth
compendium.what: Pegging the target's value to their usefulness or compliance.
compendium.why: Installs a worth-meter the speaker controls.
compendium.healthy: "I need X from you" — a need, with the person's worth left out of it.
sounds: You're only worth something when you're useful.
Earn your place in this family.
nots: May echo how the speaker was raised — repeating conditioning rather than wielding it deliberately.

compendium.name: Learned Helplessness
compendium.what: Repeatedly asserting the target cannot cope alone.
compendium.why: Said often enough, it gets believed — and then it becomes true.
compendium.healthy: "You've handled hard things before. This one's yours too, and I'm here."
sounds: You can't survive without me.
You'd fall apart in a week on your own.
nots: Anxious over-protection can produce this exact sentence with loving intent and harmful effect.

compendium.name: Loyalty Binds
compendium.what: Defining loyalty as unconditional compliance and silence.
compendium.why: Dissent becomes betrayal; the target can't disagree and stay 'good'.
compendium.healthy: "Loyalty to me includes telling me when I'm wrong."
sounds: If you tell anyone, you're betraying this family.
What happens in this house stays in this house.
nots: Loyalty is a real virtue people invoke sincerely; the flag is loyalty defined as never questioning.

compendium.name: Legal/Administrative Threats
compendium.what: Threatening police, lawyers, HR, or authorities as leverage.
compendium.why: Imports institutional force into a personal dispute to compel compliance.
compendium.healthy: Using institutions for their actual purpose — safety and rights — not as a club in an argument.
sounds: I'll have my lawyer bury you.
One call to HR and you're finished.
nots: Sometimes contacting authorities is the legitimate, correct move; the flag is the threat used as pressure ('unless you…').

compendium.name: Weaponized Therapy-Speak
compendium.what: Using clinical vocabulary as ammunition rather than understanding.
compendium.why: Borrowed authority pathologizes the target's normal responses.
compendium.healthy: Therapy language used on oneself: "I notice I'm getting defensive."
sounds: I'm setting a boundary: you're not allowed to be upset.
Your 'anxiety' is just manipulation — I've read about people like you.
nots: Therapy concepts are mainstream now; many people use them earnestly and imprecisely, not strategically.

compendium.name: Trash-Can Diagnosis
compendium.what: Assigning the target a mental-health label as an insult or verdict.
compendium.why: A diagnosis-as-weapon dismisses everything the target says as symptoms.
compendium.healthy: "I'm finding your behavior really hard" — behavior, not diagnosis.
sounds: You're a textbook narcissist.
This is your BPD talking, not you.
nots: 'You need help' can also be genuine, poorly-delivered concern for someone who's struggling.

compendium.name: Stalking-by-Notification
compendium.what: Auditing the target's online activity as evidence against them.
compendium.why: Every green dot becomes prosecutable; the target curates their existence.
compendium.healthy: "I felt low when I saw you online and hadn't heard back — irrational maybe, but real."
sounds: I saw you were online at 2am.
You posted a story but couldn't answer me?
nots: A single hurt observation about being ignored is a feeling report, not surveillance.

compendium.name: Baiting
compendium.what: Provoking a reaction to then use the reaction against the target.
compendium.why: The target's response becomes the 'evidence' — the provocation disappears from the story.
compendium.healthy: "I can see you're upset — I'd rather hear it than poke at it."
sounds: What, are you going to cry now?
There she goes again.
nots: Some of these lines are careless taunting in a mutual fight rather than a deliberate trap.

compendium.name: Interrogation
compendium.what: Demanding justification as an entitlement, on command.
compendium.why: Being made to justify, argue, defend and explain on demand trains reflexive self-defense (the JADE loop).
compendium.healthy: "Help me understand what happened?" — a question, not a summons.
sounds: You owe me an explanation.
Explain yourself. Now.
nots: Wanting an explanation after a genuine breach of trust is reasonable; the flag is the entitled, on-command framing.
Wanting a real explanation after a genuine breach of trust is fair; the flag is entitled, on-command demand.

compendium.name: Financial Enmeshment
compendium.what: Using money and assets as an instrument of control.
compendium.why: Financial control is one of the strongest practical barriers to leaving an unhealthy situation.
compendium.healthy: Transparent shared budgeting both people can see and veto.
sounds: My money, my rules.
You'll get your allowance when you behave.
nots: Households genuinely do have one earner and shared rules — the flag is money framed as leverage over behavior, not budgeting.

compendium.name: The Exception Script
compendium.what: Separating the target from peer solidarity by declaring them uniquely different, binding their identity to staying special in the manipulator's eyes.
compendium.why: If your worth depends on being 'not like the others,' criticizing the manipulator or rejoining your peers threatens your whole sense of specialness.
compendium.healthy: "I like how you think about this" — praise that doesn't require distancing you from anyone else.
sounds: You're not like the others, you actually get it.
You're different — everyone else just doesn't understand.
nots: Genuine, specific compliments exist and don't always carry an isolating agenda — the flag is the implied contrast with 'everyone else.'

compendium.name: "You're Too Emotional"
compendium.what: Using someone's emotional signal itself to disqualify them as a credible witness to their own experience.
compendium.why: It teaches the target to distrust and suppress their own reactions rather than examine what caused them.
compendium.healthy: "You seem really upset — help me understand what's going on for you."
sounds: You're too emotional to talk about this right now.
You're being so emotional about this, it's clouding your judgment.
nots: Sometimes emotional intensity really does make a conversation hard to have productively — the flag is when the emotion becomes the whole subject instead of the issue that caused it.

compendium.name: Gotcha Framing
compendium.what: Reframing an honest, exploratory statement as a confession, weaponizing the target's own transparency against them.
compendium.why: It punishes honesty, teaching the target to stop thinking out loud or admitting uncertainty.
compendium.healthy: "Thanks for being honest about that — let's figure out what to do next."
sounds: Aha, so you admit it.
So you're confessing you were there after all.
nots: Genuinely holding someone to something they said is fair; the flag is treating an exploratory or uncertain statement as a locked-in confession.

compendium.name: False Authority
compendium.what: Presenting subjective opinion or bias as neutral, unchallengeable fact.
compendium.why: It shuts down disagreement by making the target feel they're arguing with reality itself, not a person's viewpoint.
compendium.healthy: "Here's my take, and I recognize it's one perspective."
sounds: I'm just being objective here.
I'm stating facts, not opinions — you're the one being emotional.
nots: People sometimes say 'I'm being objective' sincerely, especially after real effort to set aside bias — the flag is using the claim to end a conversation rather than open one.

compendium.name: Confidentiality as Weapon
compendium.what: Invoking 'confidentiality' to block the target from seeing the evidence or accusations against them.
compendium.why: It makes real self-defense structurally impossible — you can't respond to a case you're not allowed to see.
compendium.healthy: "Here's what's been raised, and here's what I legally/ethically can and can't share — let's talk through it."
sounds: We can't share those details with you.
That's confidential, I can't tell you who complained.
nots: Real privacy and legal confidentiality obligations exist and are legitimate — the flag is confidentiality invoked specifically to prevent the target's defense, not to protect a third party.

compendium.name: Pressure to Sign
compendium.what: Pushing someone to accept documents, agreements, or blame on the spot, without time to review or consult anyone.
compendium.why: Removing time removes the ability to think clearly, get advice, or notice unfavorable terms.
compendium.healthy: "Take the weekend to read this over and ask any questions before you sign."
sounds: Sign it now, we don't have time to go over it.
You need to sign this today, before you leave the building.
nots: Some deadlines are genuinely real and external (a contract expiring, a legal filing date) — the flag is artificial urgency manufactured to prevent review.

compendium.name: Role Reversal via Therapy Language
compendium.what: Using clinical-sounding language to reframe the target's self-protection as the actual problem.
compendium.why: It borrows the credibility of therapeutic language to disarm exactly the self-protective instinct therapy is supposed to strengthen.
compendium.healthy: "I hear that you're protecting yourself — can we talk about what's making that necessary?"
sounds: That's not a boundary, that's control.
That's not self-care, that's avoidance.
nots: Sometimes what looks like a boundary really is avoidance, and a good friend or therapist might name that — the flag is this framing used to shut down a legitimate limit, not offered as caring reflection.

compendium.name: False Equivalence
compendium.what: Flattening clearly asymmetric harm into 'we both made mistakes' so responsibility looks evenly shared.
compendium.why: It erases the actual difference in who did what, making accountability impossible to land anywhere.
compendium.healthy: "I did X, which was wrong, separate from anything you did."
sounds: We both made mistakes here.
We're both equally to blame, honestly.
nots: Some conflicts really are mutual and both people did contribute — the flag is using the phrase specifically to avoid naming a clearly larger harm.

compendium.name: Aftercare Control
compendium.what: Reframing harm as help after the fact — 'that was for your own good' — so the target doubts their own read of what happened.
compendium.why: It converts the target's memory of harm into gratitude, preventing them from naming it as harm at all.
compendium.healthy: "I'm sorry that hurt you — that wasn't okay, regardless of my intentions."
sounds: That was for your own good.
You'll understand this was necessary, one day.
nots: Some hard choices really were for someone's benefit (a parent enforcing a curfew) — the flag is this phrase used to erase real pain rather than to explain a reasonable decision made in good faith.

compendium.name: Clinical Tone Policing
compendium.what: Using clinical or institutional authority to minimize real distress by framing it as excessive.
compendium.why: When the person with institutional power calls your reaction 'catastrophizing,' you have nowhere higher to appeal.
compendium.healthy: "This sounds really distressing — let's go through what we know and what we don't."
sounds: Let's not catastrophize.
You're being a bit dramatic about your symptoms.
nots: Clinicians do sometimes need to gently redirect genuine catastrophizing that's making a person's actual situation harder — the flag is when it's used to dismiss reasonable concern rather than address it.

compendium.name: False Conclusion from Normal Labs
compendium.what: Using normal test results to dismiss the reality of ongoing symptoms — 'the numbers look fine' — when the numbers don't capture the problem.
compendium.why: It tells the patient their own lived experience is less real than a metric, delaying diagnosis and validation.
compendium.healthy: "Your labs are normal, and I still believe something is wrong — let's look further."
sounds: Your labs came back completely normal.
There's nothing showing up on your scans.
nots: Normal results genuinely do rule out many things and a doctor explaining that isn't automatically dismissive — the flag is when normal results end the conversation instead of continuing it.

compendium.name: Medical Gaslighting
compendium.what: Dismissing symptoms or pain in a clinical setting so the patient's body is disbelieved by the system meant to treat it.
compendium.why: It delays real diagnosis and teaches patients — especially those from groups historically dismissed by medicine — to distrust their own symptoms.
compendium.healthy: "I don't have an answer yet, but I believe something is happening and we'll keep looking."
sounds: It's probably just anxiety.
There's nothing medically wrong with you.
nots: Anxiety and stress are real and sometimes are the correct explanation — the flag is reaching for that explanation without genuinely ruling out alternatives first.

compendium.name: Sexual Coercion
compendium.what: Using pressure, guilt, power, or implied consequences to override someone's sexual consent.
compendium.why: It makes consent conditional on avoiding punishment rather than freely given — which is not consent.
compendium.healthy: A healthy dynamic treats "no" as a complete sentence, every time, with zero relational cost.
sounds: You owe me this much.
If you really loved me, you'd do this.
nots: This tool's evidence bar here is high on purpose — but if any of this resonates, it deserves a real conversation with someone you trust or a professional, not just a private reread of this page.

compendium.name: Financial Control
compendium.what: Restricting someone's access to money, financial information, earning capacity, or economic independence to enforce dependence.
compendium.why: Financial control is one of the strongest practical barriers to leaving an unsafe or unhappy situation.
compendium.healthy: Shared, transparent finances that both people can see and neither can unilaterally lock the other out of.
sounds: You don't need your own bank account.
I'll decide what you get to spend.
nots: Genuinely agreed household budgeting with one person tracking the books isn't control by itself — the flag is unilateral restriction imposed as leverage, not shared agreement.

compendium.name: Weaponized Incompetence
compendium.what: Performing inability at unwanted tasks so they permanently land on someone else.
looks: 'You're just better at it' as a permanent division of labor.
Tasks done deliberately badly once, then never assigned again.
nots: Real skill gaps, disability, ADHD, and honest 'I don't know how' are everywhere. Intent is invisible in text — that's why this is watch-only (severity 1, never scored).
sounds: 'You're just better at it' as a permanent division of labor.
Tasks done deliberately badly once, then never assigned again.

compendium.name: Strategic Apathy
compendium.what: Cultivated indifference ('whatever', 'do what you want') used to force the other person to carry all decisions and their blame.
looks: Refusal to state any preference, followed by criticism of whatever was chosen.
'I don't care' deployed precisely at decision points.
nots: Depression, burnout, and decision fatigue produce identical sentences sincerely. Text cannot distinguish them — watch-only, never scored.
sounds: Refusal to state any preference, followed by criticism of whatever was chosen.
'I don't care' deployed precisely at decision points.

compendium.name: Reverse Psychology
compendium.what: Advocating the opposite of the desired outcome so resistance does the manipulator's work.
looks: 'You probably couldn't handle it anyway' before a wanted commitment.
'Fine, don't come' delivered as a dare.
nots: Playful challenge and genuine reverse-preference are indistinguishable from manipulation in text — watch-only, never scored.
sounds: 'You probably couldn't handle it anyway' before a wanted commitment.
'Fine, don't come' delivered as a dare.

compendium.name: Malicious Compliance
compendium.what: Following a request to the exact letter in a way deliberately designed to produce failure, while remaining technically obedient.
looks: A task completed in a way that satisfies the literal words of a request while clearly defeating its purpose.
"You told me to do X, so I did exactly X" delivered with visible satisfaction at the resulting failure.
nots: Genuine literal-minded communication (common and healthy, including for many neurodivergent communicators) produces identical-looking outcomes without any hostile intent — text alone can't distinguish deliberate sabotage from a real misunderstanding, so this stays watch-only.
sounds: A task completed in a way that satisfies the literal words of a request while clearly defeating its purpose.
"You told me to do X, so I did exactly X" delivered with visible satisfaction at the resulting failure.

compendium.name: Moral Licensing
compendium.what: Using a 'good' identity or past good deeds as informal immunity from accountability for present harm.
looks: "I'm one of the good ones" or a résumé of past virtue offered in place of addressing a specific, current complaint.
nots: People reasonably do bring up relevant context about their character or history — the flag is using that context to end scrutiny rather than to inform it, which is a judgment call text alone can't safely make.
sounds: "I'm one of the good ones" or a résumé of past virtue offered in place of addressing a specific, current complaint.

compendium.name: Strategic Self-Deprecation / Performed Humility
compendium.what: Performing self-criticism or modesty specifically to disarm defenses and pre-empt incoming critique, so the target ends up reassuring the manipulator instead of raising their concern.
looks: Self-deprecating comments that reliably appear right before or during moments the person might otherwise be criticized.
The target frequently finds themselves comforting the person who was about to be held accountable.
nots: Genuine humility and self-deprecating humor are common, healthy, and extremely hard to distinguish from a strategic version in text — this stays watch-only because the same words mean very different things depending on timing and intent that a phrase-matcher cannot see.
sounds: Self-deprecating comments that reliably appear right before or during moments the person might otherwise be criticized.
The target frequently finds themselves comforting the person who was about to be held accountable.

compendium.name: Priming / Narrative Seeding
compendium.what: Subtly installing a frame before an encounter so all subsequent information gets filtered through a lens the target never consciously chose.
looks: A pointed comment or story shared right before an event that quietly shapes how the event gets interpreted afterward.
nots: This requires comparing what was said before an event to what happened after — a single pasted message can't show the 'before,' making this fundamentally unreliable to detect from one snippet of text.
sounds: A pointed comment or story shared right before an event that quietly shapes how the event gets interpreted afterward.

compendium.name: Ambiguity as Weapon
compendium.what: Keeping exclusion, intent, or meaning deliberately vague so the target can't confirm what's happening and defaults to self-doubt.
looks: Behavior that could mean exclusion or could mean nothing — vague enough that naming it out loud sounds paranoid.
nots: By definition, this tactic is engineered to be indistinguishable from an innocent ambiguous situation in the moment — which is exactly why a phrase-matcher scoring it would be unreliable; it's included here for literacy, not detection.
sounds: Behavior that could mean exclusion or could mean nothing — vague enough that naming it out loud sounds paranoid.

compendium.name: Push-Pull
compendium.what: Alternating warmth and coldness in cycles — closeness offered, then withdrawn, then offered again — keeping the target chasing the warm version.
looks: Affectionate messages followed by sudden distance without explanation, repeatedly.
The temperature of the conversation swings on the manipulator's schedule, not events.
nots: People genuinely run hot and cold under stress, illness, or depression — the flag is a repeating cycle that resets whenever the target starts to pull away.
sounds: Affectionate messages followed by sudden distance without explanation, repeatedly.

compendium.name: Intermittent Reinforcement
compendium.what: Rewards (affection, approval, kindness) delivered unpredictably and rarely, which conditions stronger attachment than consistent kindness ever could.
looks: Long stretches of criticism or indifference punctuated by occasional, intense warmth.
The target works harder and harder for rarer and rarer good moments.
nots: Inconsistency from a chaotic life is not a strategy — the flag is warmth that reliably appears exactly when the target is about to disengage.
sounds: Long stretches of criticism or indifference punctuated by occasional, intense warmth.

compendium.name: Breadcrumbing
compendium.what: Minimal, sporadic attention — just enough contact to keep someone available and hoping, with no intention of real investment. (Absorbs 'Benching': keeping someone on the roster with periodic pings.)
looks: Occasional low-effort messages ('hey stranger', a like, an emoji) after long silence, never converting to plans.
Warmth spikes whenever the target seems to be moving on.
nots: Busy people drift and ping sporadically without strategy — the flag is a stable pattern where contact exists only to prevent detachment, never to build anything.
sounds: Occasional low-effort messages ('hey stranger', a like, an emoji) after long silence, never converting to plans.

compendium.name: Trauma Bonding
compendium.what: An attachment forged by the cycle of harm followed by relief — the person causing the pain is also the one providing comfort, fusing fear and love.
looks: Intense reconciliations after intense harm, described as proof of how deep the connection is.
Feeling most attached right after the worst episodes.
nots: Strong bonds forged through shared hardship (illness, grief) are not trauma bonds — the flag is when the hardship is caused by the partner and the relief is dispensed by them.
sounds: Intense reconciliations after intense harm, described as proof of how deep the connection is.

compendium.name: Relief Bait
compendium.what: A brief dose of kindness dropped immediately after harm, so the target's nervous system associates the manipulator with relief and tolerance resets.
looks: Cruelty followed within hours by uncharacteristic sweetness, gifts, or tenderness — then the cycle repeats.
The 'good moments' cluster suspiciously right after the bad ones.
nots: Genuine repair after conflict includes acknowledgment and changed behavior; relief bait skips the acknowledgment and changes nothing.
sounds: Cruelty followed within hours by uncharacteristic sweetness, gifts, or tenderness — then the cycle repeats.

compendium.name: Withholding
compendium.what: Strategic removal of affection, attention, information, or communication as leverage — a punishment that leaves no visible mark.
looks: Warmth, answers, or basic acknowledgment disappear whenever the target displeases, and return when they comply.
Questions met with meaningful silence across many exchanges.
nots: Needing space, shutting down under overwhelm, or slow replies during a hard week are human — the flag is withdrawal that reliably tracks compliance.
sounds: Warmth, answers, or basic acknowledgment disappear whenever the target displeases, and return when they comply.

compendium.name: Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde
compendium.what: Two dramatically different personas — charming in public or in good phases, cruel in private or in bad ones — so the target doubts which one is real and outsiders doubt the target.
looks: Message history swings between two unrecognizably different voices.
Witnesses see only the charming version; the target has screenshots of the other.
nots: Mood variation, masking, and stress responses are normal — the flag is the strategic placement of each persona (charm for witnesses, cruelty for the target).
sounds: Message history swings between two unrecognizably different voices.

compendium.name: Ambient Abuse
compendium.what: A background atmosphere of tension, criticism, and unpredictability rather than discrete incidents — no single message looks damning, but the climate is corrosive.
looks: No individual line is extreme, yet reading the whole thread feels like walking on eggshells.
Constant low-grade correction, sighing disapproval, and conditional moods.
nots: A stressed household or blunt communication culture can feel tense without being abusive — the flag is that the tension consistently serves one person's control.

compendium.name: Ghosting-Orbiting Cycle
compendium.what: Disappearing from direct contact while continuing to watch and lightly touch the target's digital life (views, likes, reactions) — absence with surveillance.
looks: No replies for weeks, but every story viewed within minutes.
Reappearing with a small reaction whenever the target seems to be moving on.
nots: Passive scrolling by someone who simply drifted away isn't a campaign — the flag is the timing correlation with the target's recovery.

compendium.name: Stonewalling
compendium.what: Complete, repeated refusal to engage, respond, or resolve — silence deployed as punishment and erasure rather than genuine processing time.
looks: Every attempt to discuss an issue is met with total non-engagement, repeatedly, across many messages.
Requests for even a timeline to talk are also refused.
nots: A single 'I need space right now, can we talk tomorrow' is healthy self-regulation, not stonewalling — the flag is a repeating pattern of refusal with no return offered, not one instance of needing a pause.

compendium.name: Sealioning
compendium.what: Persistent, bad-faith requests for evidence, sources, or explanation — not to understand, but to exhaust the target until they give up trying to be heard.
looks: Every point is met with 'source?' or 'prove it' rather than engagement with the substance.
The questions never stop, no matter how much evidence is provided.
nots: Genuinely wanting evidence before believing something serious is reasonable — the flag is a bottomless pattern of demands that never resolves into actual engagement, no matter what's provided.

compendium.name: Idealize-Devalue-Discard Cycle
compendium.what: The complete arc of elevation, systematic devaluation, and disposal — often repeating with a new person receiving the identical idealization script.
looks: An opening period of intense, almost scripted-feeling admiration, followed by a slow reversal into criticism and eventual discard.
If there's a 'replacement,' they may describe an eerily similar opening phase.
nots: Relationships naturally move from an infatuation phase into a calmer, more realistic one — that's normal and healthy. The flag is a full cycle ending in disposal, especially if it has happened before with a similar script.

compendium.name: Extinction Bursts
compendium.what: A dramatic escalation in manipulation tactics precisely when a previously effective method stops working — the last, loudest attempt before an old strategy is abandoned.
looks: A sudden spike in intensity or a new, harsher tactic appearing right after the target successfully resisted or set a boundary for the first time.
"This has never happened before" moments that follow a clear act of resistance.
nots: People do sometimes get more upset right after a hard conversation for ordinary reasons — the flag is a spike that specifically follows successful resistance and is aimed at re-establishing the old dynamic.

compendium.name: Competitive Victimhood
compendium.what: Responding to the target's pain with a bigger pain of one's own, ensuring the target's experience never receives full attention.
looks: Every time you raise something that hurt you, the conversation ends up about how much worse it's been for them.

nots: Sometimes someone really is going through something bigger and it's fair for that to come up — the flag is a reliable pattern where your pain is never allowed room of its own.

compendium.name: Ambient Sexual Threat
compendium.what: Maintaining a sexually charged or threatening atmosphere without any single overt act, keeping the target hypervigilant with nothing concrete to point to.
looks: A pattern of comments, looks described secondhand, or 'jokes' that consistently leave you uneasy, across many separate incidents.
You find yourself managing your schedule or location around this person without being able to say exactly why.
nots: A single tasteless joke, especially if apologized for, isn't this pattern — the flag is a sustained climate across many incidents that a reasonable person would find unsettling.

compendium.name: "Polite Hostile" Environments
compendium.what: A workplace or social space that appears civil and professional on its surface while systematically punishing truth-telling, dissent, or authenticity underneath.
looks: Every formal interaction is impeccably polite, yet raising real concerns is consistently followed by subtle exclusion, cooled relationships, or stalled opportunities.
Colleagues describe a 'vibe' they can't quite name in official terms.
nots: Genuine workplace civility and professionalism are good things — the flag is politeness used specifically as camouflage for a retaliation pattern, visible only once you track outcomes over months.

compendium.name: Self-Gaslighting Induction
compendium.what: The installed habit of doubting your own memory and perception before anyone else has to — the endpoint of sustained gaslighting.
looks: Catching yourself saying 'maybe I'm remembering it wrong' about things you documented.

compendium.name: Fawning
compendium.what: A survival response of appeasing and pleasing a threatening person — agreement, flattery, and self-erasure as safety strategy.
looks: Apologizing for things that were done to you.

nots: Kindness, diplomacy, and conflict-avoidance are personality, not pathology. Fawning is specifically fear-driven appeasement of a particular person.

As a communication pattern, Gaslighting-type behavior in the Reality Distortion category tends to work by targeting confidence in one's own memory or perception, so the person starts checking their read of events against the other person's account instead of their own — describing a pattern in the exchange, not a fixed trait in the person.

codex_completed.why_this_matters: Repeated reality-denial erodes a person's trust in their own judgment. Naming a pattern accurately — without over-claiming — is usually what restores clarity faster than either ignoring it or catastrophizing it.
what_it_is: Denying someone's perception or memory to make them doubt their own mind.
Repeated reality-denial erodes a person's trust in their own judgment.
Falls under the Reality Distortion category in this project's taxonomy.

innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: Genuine memory differences about ambiguous events are common and don't require any intent to distort.

common_false_positives: Genuine, good-faith uncertainty about an ambiguous shared memory, expressed as a real difference rather than flat denial.

discernment_questions: Does the denial apply to something with clear, independent evidence, or is it about a genuinely ambiguous memory?

less_concerning_if: The disagreement is about something genuinely ambiguous, with openness to checking evidence together.
more_concerning_if: Denial applies to something with clear evidence and recurs as a pattern, without willingness to verify.
pattern_over_time_signs: The same behavior repeats across multiple separate conversations.

The intensity or frequency increases over time rather than resolving.
Other tactics from a similar category start appearing alongside it.

codex_completed.boundary_respect_check: When a boundary was stated plainly in this area, was it honored going forward — or tested, ignored, punished, or reframed as unreasonable? Boundary respect observed over multiple instances is one of the more reliable signals available.

codex_completed.possible_impact_on_receiver: People sometimes describe increased self-doubt, difficulty trusting one's own memory, and a growing habit of deferring to someone else's account of events in connection with patterns like this. Impact varies widely by person, history, and context — this is a possibility to consider, not a predicted or universal outcome, and it is not a diagnosis of the person on the receiving end of a sustained pattern like this.

response_options.firm_boundary: State a clear boundary and observe whether it's respected going forward, without over-explaining or justifying it.
response_options.disengagement: It's reasonable to step back from a specific conversation or topic rather than continuing to press it in the moment.
response_options.support_seeking: Talk it through with someone outside the situation before deciding how to respond.
response_options.workplace_or_professional: In a workplace context, document what happened factually and know your organization's reporting channels (HR, a manager, an ombudsperson) before escalating.

codex_completed.core_meaning: Structuring information so no one person can see the full picture, limiting accountability and oversight.
codex_completed.short_definition: Structuring information so no one person can see the full picture, limiting accountability and oversight.
codex_completed.expanded_definition: Structuring information — in a family, workplace, or organization — so that no single person has access to the full picture, which has the effect of limiting anyone's ability to hold the person controlling the information accountable, since no one else can see enough to connect the dots. Each individual piece of information may be shared honestly; the deception lives in how the pieces are kept apart.
codex_completed.plain_language_summary: In plain terms: structuring information so no one person can see the full picture, limiting accountability and oversight.
codex_completed.why_this_matters: Patterns like this can shape communication, trust, and decision-making — left unnamed, they can contribute to misplaced trust in a distorted picture of a situation, discovered later, if at all. Naming a pattern accurately — without over-claiming — is usually what restores clarity faster than either ignoring it or catastrophizing it.

innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: Legitimate confidentiality and natural information silos exist in most families and organizations without any intent to avoid accountability. Not proactively sharing everything with everyone isn't automatically a control tactic.
common_false_positives: Legitimate confidentiality or need-to-know structures that exist for genuinely appropriate reasons.
Natural information silos that develop in any large family or organization without deliberate intent to prevent accountability.
A person simply not thinking to share information broadly, rather than deliberately withholding it from specific people.
discernment_questions: Is there a legitimate reason for the information to be compartmentalized, or does it seem to specifically prevent accountability?
Does connecting the compartmentalized pieces reveal something the person controlling the information wouldn't want revealed?
Are people actively discouraged from comparing notes, or does that discouragement just happen not to occur?
Would this person be uncomfortable if the full picture were assembled and shared openly?
less_concerning_if: Any compartmentalization has a legitimate, non-accountability-avoiding reason.
more_concerning_if: The compartmentalization specifically prevents anyone from seeing a pattern that would otherwise be concerning, and connecting information is discouraged.

recipes.d: Staged sequence that lowers defenses, tests compliance, accelerates attachment, and installs dependency before exploitation begins.
Creates neurochemical dependency through a dopamine-cortisol cycle — target becomes addicted to the relief, not the person.
Fuses the target to the source of their pain — each abuse cycle followed by enough warmth to trigger bonding, creating attachment that strengthens with every cycle.
Engineers the perception of a perfect, destined connection by reflecting everything the target wants — leaving feels like spiritual loss.
Transforms the target's empathy into a leash — their compassion is weaponized so any boundary feels like cruelty.
One-directional extraction disguised as mutual care — the imbalance only reveals itself when the target stops giving.
Alternates between elevation and diminishment to create dependency on the manipulator's approval.
What was promised bears no resemblance to what's delivered — but by the time reality is clear, leaving costs more than staying.
Every gift creates a debt, every debt requires gratitude, gratitude creates new expectations, unmet expectations generate guilt — perpetual invisible obligation.
Target must perform continuous thankfulness as the price of belonging — any complaint is met with "after everything we've done for you."
Manipulator becomes the target's only source of comfort and safety — then uses that dependency to ensure the target returns to the source of harm.

via Self-Harm Threats The master combo — multi-layered system making departure feel more dangerous, costly, and terrifying than staying across financial, emotional, psychological, and social barriers simultaneously.
Imprisonment inside comfort — the cage is beautiful, the benefits are real, leaving is catastrophic, and wanting out feels ungrateful because the bars are made of privilege.
Compensation calibrated to be just generous enough to make freedom unaffordable — trapped not by poverty but by prosperity that can't be replicated elsewhere.
Interconnected network of debts, duties, and expectations so dense that cutting one thread tightens three others — no single obligation is insurmountable but the web is inescapable.
Multi-dimensional entanglement across financial, social, emotional, informational, and identity structures ensuring the target cannot survive independently.
Complete architecture ensuring the target cannot survive without the system — independence eliminated, alternatives removed, information restricted, health compromised, just enough comfort provided.
Financial obligations structured so they cannot be resolved, discharged, or escaped — the debt itself becomes the control mechanism.
Punishment of Disloyalty Weaponizes the target's loyalty — departure is reframed as betrayal, and visible punishment of defectors teaches everyone still inside the cost of leaving.
Installs guilt so deep it becomes the primary governing force — the target feels responsible for the manipulator's wellbeing, silencing their own advocacy.
Fuses the target's identity to the institution so thoroughly that departure feels like self-destruction — they can't imagine who they'd be without it.
Uses prior investment as prison bars — the more invested, the harder to leave, not because the future is promising but because the past is too expensive to write off.
Doesn't prevent leaving — destroys the world behind you so departure feels like exile rather than liberation.
Uses someone the target loves as leverage — the target's protective instinct becomes the weapon that keeps them silent.
Trains behavioral responses through unpredictable reward and strategic pain removal upon compliance — the nervous system is programmed to associate obedience with safety.
Installs reflex compliance through meaningless rules, disproportionate consequences, and visible punishment — the content is irrelevant; unquestioning submission is the product.
Creates chronic hypervigilance — the target's entire capacity is consumed by monitoring the manipulator's mood, leaving nothing for self-advocacy or escape.
Incremental escalation so gradual no single step triggers alarm — conditions worsen one degree at a time until the unthinkable becomes the tolerated.
Every channel of self-expression is systematically mined with consequences until silence becomes the only safe option.
Contradictory demands coexist, success is redefined after achievement, and the target's inevitable failure is framed as personal deficiency rather than the system's design.
Target cannot win — losses are their fault, wins belong to someone else, and the game appears fair from outside while every mechanism is calibrated to produce failure.
Forces the target to prove allegiance under pressure — hesitation is treated as betrayal; the purpose is to deepen submission through forced demonstration of compliance.
Engineers dependency on external validation by alternating praise and criticism while fusing self-worth to the manipulator's opinion — internal self- worth is replaced.
Extracts maximum effort while delivering minimum return — always promising the reward is just ahead, celebrating just enough to sustain hope, moving the finish line every time.
Systematic depletion through relentless demands, shifting expectations, manufactured crises, and moral framing that makes rest feel like failure — then diagnoses the burnout as personal weakness.

Multi-layered obedience system — arbitrary rules build the habit, inconsistent rewards create the drive, visible consequences teach the group, and demonstrations of total power eliminate belief that resistance is possible.
Rapid unpredictable oscillation between extremes of warmth and coldness — dysregulates the nervous system until stability feels boring and chaos feels like passion.
Graduated small asks paired with reinforcement until compliance becomes self-sustaining — the external enforcer is no longer needed because obedience has become identity.
Institutional reward systems replace intrinsic motivation with extrinsic dependency — the target performs not for meaning but for the next measurable reward.
Gradually escalates harmful conditions while training the target to absorb each escalation as the new baseline — the Overton Window shifts until the unacceptable becomes unremarkable.

Extinguishes belief that actions can produce change through repeated futile effort — the target stops trying not because they don't care but because they've been trained to believe effort is pointless.
Installs an internal standard so impossibly high the target exists in permanent inadequacy — always striving, never arriving, interpreting rest as proof of falling behind.

"Just Following Orders" Escalating moral compromises, each small enough to justify individually but devastating in accumulation — the target ends up doing things they would have refused outright at the start.
Comprehensively destabilizes the target’s certainty until “I know” becomes “I think.”
Erases the original event and installs an institutionally supported alternative reality.
Overwhelms cognition so the target abandons their original question and accepts whatever ends the confusion.
Deletes evidence, witnesses, and documentation until the event “never happened.”
Rewrites the target’s identity so the messenger becomes the problem, not the message.
Creates lose-lose contradictions so the target doubts their judgment and defers to authority.
Installs interpretive lenses before information is encountered so the target’s “thoughts” aren’t theirs.
Steals positive language and repurposes it to sell harmful practices the target would never agree to.
Creates a persistent gap between stated and lived reality so the target stops trusting their own perception.
Reverses the direction of a complaint so the reporter becomes the investigated and the official record reflects the institution's counter-narrative, not the original concern.

Full-spectrum accountability reversal where the accused denies, attacks, files counter-complaints, performs victimhood, cries to shut down questioning, and destroys the reporter's credibility — producing a complete inversion where the harmer is comforted and the harmed is investigated.

Performs remorse without delivering change — a vague apology is paired with sympathy-redirecting explanations, the harmer controls the timing and terms of reconciliation, the target is pressured to move on, nothing structurally changes, and the neurochemical relief of the apology resets the cycle.

Eight-layer defense system where each layer redirects, reflects, confuses, or absorbs accountability — no single layer needs to stop you completely, each just slows you enough for the next to engage, until the demand dissolves and the person responsible is untouchable.

Master combo where accountability enters the system and never exits — responsibility is distributed until it dissolves, every individual performed their function without producing a result, processes exhaust the complainant across years, and institutional documentation repurposes the complaint as evidence of responsiveness.

Control, criticism, and professional destruction wrapped in care — each attack is individually defensible as mentorship, emotional responses are used as proof of the deficit being named, identity-level shame is installed as wisdom, and public warmth makes the private destruction unspeakable.

via Implicit Consequence Genuine or performed emotion deployed as a tactical barrier at the precise moment accountability arrives — pain redirects the room, the person seeking accountability becomes the comforter, a vague self-admission preempts specific demands, and the target's own empathy becomes the cage that prevents the question from being asked.

Control exercised so smoothly that naming it makes the target sound paranoid — composure makes any emotional response disproportionate, every directive is framed as a suggestion, public warmth contradicts private complaints, and the target's autonomy is systematically narrowed while every narrowing feels like care.

A threat delivered so softly it cannot be quoted or reported — institutional precarity is mentioned in proximity to the target's behavior, calm delivery makes the fear response seem irrational, legitimate processes are implied as consequences, and deliberate ambiguity forces the target to fill in the blanks with their own worst-case scenario.

Confidential complaint leaked to activate community members who deliver institutional pressure without institutional fingerprints — multiple contacts apply converging pressure across days, the institution claims no involvement, the complaint is reframed as community disruption, and every contact carries the same implicit message: drop it.
